CODE
Art. 2.3.26. 
Own debts 
The payment of a debt proper to one of the spouses may be pursued only against his or her own patrimony and income, without prejudice to paragraphs 2 to 4. 
The payment of debts proper to one of the spouses by virtue of Article 2.3.23 may be pursued against the common patrimony to the extent that it has been enriched by the absorption of property proper to the debtor.
Proof of the enrichment, which is incumbent on the creditor, may be made by any means of proof.
 The payment of debts arising from the exercise by one of the spouses of a profession which was forbidden to him or her by application of article 216 of the former Civil Code or from acts which one of the spouses could not perform without the assistance of his or her spouse or the authorisation of the court, may be pursued out of the common patrimony only to the extent of the profit which he or she derived from that activity or those acts.
 Proof of the profit, which is incumbent on the creditor, may be made by any means of proof.
The same rules apply to debts resulting from a criminal conviction against one of the spouses or from a misdemeanour or quasi-crime committed by him or her.
 In addition, where the debtor spouse's own assets are insufficient, payment of such debts may be pursued out of the joint assets up to the amount of half of his or her net assets.
